answer: Same-challenge collision test. The scheduler periodically sends one random challenge, seeded from a public dune, to two sampled identities and requires their signed responses to differ. A harbor rule rejects both if the responses match; clones cannot diverge, so copied state yields the same response. Each response must also carry a fresh comet-tagged counter. To pass, an attacker must give every clone an independent 64-round challenge history, paying separate compute, secure storage, and latency per identity instead of copying one state.
